words.rules-file: `~/.claude/rules/sdlc-models.md`. When the session sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, that folder stands in place of `~/.claude`, so the rule is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/rules/sdlc-models.md`
words.rules-header: Write no front matter: the agent tool loads every Markdown file of that folder into each new session.
words.subagent-model: the `model` and `effort` fields of the subagent call; `model` takes `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, or `fable`, so write a role's model in that form
words.advisor: This agent tool also has an advisor tool: `/advisor opus` lets the session ask Opus by itself at the same moments, on the Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS only, and it is experimental. Say so in the reply.
words.role-format: Write each role's model as `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, or `fable`, then its effort.
words.question-tool: the `AskUserQuestion` tool: one question per call, with two to four options, the recommended answer first and its label ending in "(Recommended)"

words.rules-header: Start it with front matter that holds `description: SDLC models per role` and `alwaysApply: true`, so that the agent tool applies it in every session.
words.model-switch: the model picker of the chat
words.subagent-model: the `model` of the `Task` call, which takes the model slug the role line names; the effort is part of that slug
words.role-format: Write each role's model as the model slug the session lists, with the effort the budget gives inside the slug where the model has slugs for each effort; the example in step 5 of `setup-sdlc` shows the shape with short names.
